ai.description: This 20–25 mm frog is brown with dark dorsal mottling and a distinct pale snout tip. It features granular skin, a white belly, and lacks webbing on its fingers and toes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes dubois* is best distinguished by its distinct, bright yellow or orange groin and hidden surfaces of the thighs, which contrast sharply with its dorsal color.
ai.habitat: Raorchestes dubois inhabits high-altitude montane shola forests and adjacent grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 1,800 and 2,400 meters.
ai.behavior: The Kodaikanal bush frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects among the leaf litter and low-lying vegetation of its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes dubois* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. They lay small clutches of terrestrial eggs in vegetation, typically during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: Raorchestes dubois is endemic to the high-altitude shola forests of the Palani Hills in Tamil Nadu, India, typically occurring at elevations above 2,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Kodaikanal Bush Frog emits a high-pitched, insect-like trill consisting of a rapid series of pulsed notes, typically heard from vegetation in high-altitude shola forests.
